channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Can Employees Refuse Work if Wages Are Delayed? A Lawyer Explains
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 34 enterprises owe employees 453.5 million tenge in wages over nine months. The State Labor Inspectorate Committee clarifies where to seek help for delayed payments. The article discusses whether employees have the right to stop working and how to claim unpaid wages.

item.title: US Flights Grounded Due to Communication System Failure at All Airports
item.description: All flights across the US were halted due to a communication system failure affecting air traffic controllers. Over 1.5 million passengers were impacted as planes were unable to take off for more than four hours. The issue stemmed from an outdated system experiencing technical difficulties.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Making Housing Insurance Mandatory for Natural Disasters
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning to introduce mandatory housing insurance against natural disasters. Currently, only 3.2% of the country's housing stock is insured, despite 75% of the territory being at risk. The proposed changes aim to create a system where funds for damage compensation are accumulated through insurance premiums.

item.title: Australian Skyscraper Transformed into Solar Power Station
item.description: A 48-story skyscraper in Melbourne, Australia, has been converted into a solar power station. The building's exterior walls and roof are now equipped with 1,391 solar panels. These panels are expected to generate up to 20% of the building's electricity needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Explains President's Address to Foreign Diplomats and International Organizations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister briefed around 100 foreign diplomats on President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address. The address outlines long-term development strategies and Kazakhstan's pragmatic foreign policy. It invites mutually beneficial cooperation, highlighting infrastructure modernization and investment protection. Key sectors for collaboration include energy, agriculture, digitalization, and water management.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prioritizes Increasing Power Sources and Modernizing Energy Infrastructure
item.description: A meeting chaired by First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlan Nalbajev reviewed the implementation of the President's directives on energy development. Discussions focused on building new power plants, gasifying settlements, and modernizing energy and utility infrastructure. Special attention was given to the Ekibastuz GRES-3 and Kurchatov coal power plant construction, and new heating plants in Kokshetau, Semey, and Oskemen.

item.title: International Criminal Court Closes Part of Afghanistan Investigation, Focuses on Taliban
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has closed a portion of its investigation into Afghanistan, shifting focus solely to the Taliban's actions since 2021. This decision means alleged crimes by US forces and the Islamic State-Khorasan group will not be pursued. The closure follows a dispute over prosecutorial strategy and US sanctions against the court. Arrest warrants for Taliban leaders remain active.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Vows to Eradicate Organized Crime
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov promised to eliminate organized crime in Kyrgyzstan during a meeting with residents. He stated that the country's international image has improved, shifting from news of crime and protests to focus on cultural events and economic growth, attracting more tourists. Japarov emphasized that the era of aspiring to be a criminal is over.

item.title: Kazakhstan People's Council Addresses Citizen Concerns on Housing and Debt
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov, Chairman of the Kazakhstan People's Council, heard citizens' requests regarding housing, debt relief, and support for honest borrowers. A resident from the Aktobe region raised issues with construction companies violating equity holders' rights. Koshanov instructed relevant ministries to expedite legal changes to resolve the matter promptly.

item.title: Kazakhstan Parliament Considers New Laws on Online Platforms and Media
item.description: The bureau of the Parliament of Kazakhstan approved the agenda for the upcoming session, including draft laws on online platforms and mass media. These amendments aim to establish legal responsibility for spreading destructive content online and create a safe digital environment for children. The Parliament also plans to review the 2027-2029 state budget.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Return of Businessman's Property
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov ordered the return of a businessman's property in Issyk-Kul, following a complaint from a resident whose husband was allegedly framed and pressured to cede assets. The businessman's family claims their property was legally acquired and built over 30 years. Japarov questioned the alleged ties to organized crime before ordering the review.

item.title: Tajikistan President Inaugurates New International Hospital in Dushanbe
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan has opened the new International Hospital in Dushanbe, a facility designed for 1200 diagnostic patients and 150 inpatients. The hospital features 30 departments equipped with modern diagnostic and treatment tools, including AI-powered equipment for precise disease diagnosis. It operates on a unified digital system and currently employs 186 specialists, with plans to expand to 420 jobs.

item.title: Shohin Airlines to Launch Domestic Flights Connecting Dushanbe with Four Cities
item.description: Shohin Airlines has announced plans to launch regular domestic flights from Dushanbe to Khorog, Khujand, Bokhtar, and Kulob. The new routes aim to develop regional air travel and improve transport accessibility within Tajikistan. The airline will use modern L410 NG aircraft with a capacity of 19 passengers, operating flights based on weather conditions. This initiative supports the country's infrastructure development goals.

item.title: Putin, Trump, and Xi Jinping to Meet in Shenzhen on November 19
item.description: A meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled for November 19 in Shenzhen. The leaders are expected to discuss a new nuclear arms control agreement, as well as the situations in Iran, North Korea, and Ukraine.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President warns against ethnic provocations ahead of elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov addressed concerns about potential ethnic provocations aimed at disrupting upcoming elections. He stated that while no organized attempts are currently underway, authorities possess information about such possibilities and are prepared to prevent them.

item.title: Uzbekistan revises 2025 GDP forecast upwards to $169 billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Statistics Committee has revised its nominal GDP figures for 2017-2025. The 2025 forecast increased from $147 billion to $169 billion, a 15% rise. This recalculation, based on updated census data and international standards, reflects a more comprehensive accounting of economic activity rather than new growth, officials stated.

item.title: US flights resume after 5-hour system outage disrupts air traffic control
item.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has lifted a nationwide ground stop after a major disruption to its air traffic control system. The outage, lasting approximately five hours, caused around 4,700 flights to be canceled and 10,000 more to be delayed. Officials cited a telecommunications infrastructure failure as the cause.

item.title: North Korean hackers stole $400 million in cryptocurrency using AI and fake video calls
item.description: North Korean hackers have stolen over $400 million in cryptocurrency in the past 18 months, employing artificial intelligence and deceptive video calls. The US Department of Justice reported that attackers impersonated acquaintances to trick victims into installing malware, leading to crypto theft. The FBI identified North Korean hacking groups behind the 'FaceStealer' scheme.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements New Apparel Labeling and Traceability Rules
item.description: New rules for labeling and traceability of light industry goods took effect in Kazakhstan on November 14, 2026. Businesses must use special DataMatrix codes to track products from production to sale. The mandatory labeling will be introduced in stages until October 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 2027 State Budget to Maintain Social Orientation, President Mirziyoyev States
item.description: Uzbekistan's state budget for 2027 will preserve its social focus, according to President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The country anticipates economic growth of at least 8% this year, with GDP exceeding $200 billion. The budget aims to enhance public welfare, access to education, and healthcare services.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Banning Social Media for Children Under 16
item.description: Kazakhstan is planning to prohibit social media registration for individuals under 16 years old. The proposed legislation, which excludes messengers, also aims to hold online platforms accountable for disseminating harmful content. This initiative is part of a broader effort to create a safer digital environment for minors.

item.title: International Scientific Conference for Young Scientists Held in Tashkent
item.description: An international scientific conference for young scientists titled 'Science and Innovation' took place at the Presidium of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan in Tashkent. The event aimed to foster scientific potential, enhance international cooperation, and share expertise in innovative developments. The conference featured 37 oral presentations and poster sessions.

item.title: Taliban Minister Orders Eviction of 500 Families from Kabul Homes
item.description: Nearly 500 families in Omid-e Sabz Township, western Kabul, have been ordered to vacate their homes by the Taliban's Minister of Justice, Abdul Hakim Sharaei. Residents face severe challenges as winter approaches, with some forced to pay rent for their own homes. Sources report widespread anxiety and difficult living conditions.

item.title: Europe Could Save 40% on Electricity Bills with Solar and Batteries
item.description: Europe could reduce electricity expenses by 40% through the combined use of solar energy and battery storage, provided these technologies are deployed effectively. Solar power has become a leading clean energy source, helping to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and mitigate price volatility. Proper integration of battery systems is crucial to prevent energy loss when production exceeds demand.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Over 18,000 Sentenced to Prison in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Uzbek courts reviewed 64,902 criminal cases involving 78,739 individuals in the first nine months of 2026. Of those convicted, 18,026 (31.4%) received prison sentences, an increase from the previous year. The Supreme Court reported that 385 individuals were acquitted, with 161 recognized as victims of repression.

item.title: WHO urges Afghanistan to resume house-to-house polio vaccinations amid rising cases
item.description: The World Health Organization is pressing Afghanistan to reinstate house-to-house polio vaccination campaigns. The country has reported 25 wild polio cases this year, exceeding last year's total. WHO warns that the current system of fixed vaccination sites is failing to reach many children, increasing the risk of further spread.

item.title: Trump discusses US policy on Iran, Cuba, and relations with Israel
item.description: In a media interview, President Trump outlined US policy towards Iran and Cuba, and discussed relations with Israel. He affirmed strong support for Israel and expressed readiness to use military force to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, not ruling out renewed large-scale operations. Trump also aims to resolve issues with Cuba before his term ends.

item.title: Uzbekistan Joins $720 Million International Climate Investment Program
item.description: Uzbekistan is now one of ten countries participating in the Transformation Pathways Initiative (TPI), an international climate investment program totaling $720 million. Launched at COP31 in Turkey, the initiative aims to provide developing nations with long-term climate finance for adopting green technologies and reducing emissions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Expand Cooperation in Youth Sphere
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are enhancing cooperation in youth affairs, with discussions held in Tashkent between the head of Rossotrudnichestvo and local students. Key topics included educational collaboration, Russian language learning, and joint youth projects. Both sides agreed to establish interaction between youth parliamentary structures.

item.title: Combating Climate Change: Our Responsibility to Future Generations
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's initiatives at the UN climate change conference highlight the urgency of environmental security and sustainable development. The focus is on implementing green economy principles, increasing renewable energy use, reducing emissions, and efficient water resource management, particularly addressing the Aral Sea ecological crisis.

item.title: US Congress Summons Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang for Testimony on National Security Concerns
item.description: The US Senate Banking Committee has invited Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify regarding national security concerns and the protection of critical technologies. Several House committees have also requested his appearance. Huang was asked to respond by November 13, with a closed-door meeting potentially scheduled for December 1.

item.title: Turkmenistan Approves Composition of Joint Intergovernmental Committee with Pakistan
item.description: To further develop cooperation and strengthen bilateral economic relations, the President of Turkmenistan has signed a decree approving the composition of the Turkmen side of the Joint Turkmen-Pakistani Intergovernmental Committee. This aims to enhance collaboration between the two nations.

item.title: Heads of Kazakhstan's Largest Sovereign Wealth Fund and National Company Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee announced the arrest of Nurlan Jakupov, head of the Samruk-Kazyna fund, and Yelyas Otinshiyev, head of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, on suspicion of corruption. Both were detained on November 11. Investigations are ongoing to determine all circumstances of the case.

item.title: Climate Finance Dominates COP31 Talks Amid Concerns Over Afghanistan’s Absence
item.description: A ministerial meeting at COP31 in Turkey focused on mobilizing climate finance for vulnerable nations. Discussions covered developing countries' access to funds, adaptation programs, and crisis response. Experts expressed concern over Afghanistan's limited representation, hindering its access to crucial financial and technical assistance.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Prioritize Digital Control and Transparency in 2027 Budget, Says Saida Mirziyoyeva
item.description: Uzbekistan's government will focus on budget transparency and digital control for the upcoming year's expenditures, according to Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration. Key tax rates will remain unchanged. The largest portion of the budget will be allocated to education, healthcare, and local community development, aiming for 7% GDP growth.

item.title: Kazakh President Tasks National Security Committee Chairman on Key Issues
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Ермек Сағымбаев, Chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB). The KNB chairman reported on the committee's activities since the beginning of the year, including efforts against terrorism, extremism, drug trafficking, and organized crime. Special attention was given to anti-corruption and cybersecurity measures. The President issued several directives.

item.title: Khiva to Host UNESCO International Symposium on Cultural Heritage Preservation in 2027
item.description: UNESCO's Executive Board has supported holding an international symposium in Khiva in 2027 on "Preservation of Cultural Heritage in the Context of Globalization and Climate Change." The event will gather experts to discuss threats to cultural heritage, modern technologies, and traditional knowledge. Recommendations for improving heritage protection methods will be developed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Orders Banks to Refund Illegal Loan Interest and Fines
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has mandated commercial banks to conduct internal audits by December 10th. Banks must identify and rectify legal violations, refunding any illegally charged loan interest and fines to borrowers. This directive follows court decisions on unlawful charges.

item.title: Kazakh Flight Attendant Contracts Unknown Illness in Kuwait, Loses Recognition
item.description: A 25-year-old Kazakh flight attendant fell ill with an unknown disease after a flight from Nepal to Kuwait. Initially recovering, her condition worsened, leading to memory loss and inability to recognize family. Kazakh diplomats assisted in her readmission to a clinic. Doctors are investigating potential causes, including Japanese encephalitis.

item.title: Sweden Shows Interest in Hiring Uzbek Citizens for Agriculture and Healthcare Sectors
item.description: Uzbekistan and Sweden are planning to enhance cooperation in vocational training to attract Uzbek specialists to the Swedish labor market. A forum in Stockholm discussed professional and language training for migrants and their legal employment abroad, highlighting Sweden's need for workers in agriculture, healthcare, and construction.
